dedupe_keys.name: nist fire calorimetry database fcd heat release rates of burning items rooms and fuels

description: The Fire Calorimetry Database holds results, data files and images of fire experiments run at the NIST National Fire Research Laboratory, whose open calorimeters measure heat release and combustion products for fires from 50 kW to 20,000 kW. Specimens include single burning items, fully furnished rooms, controlled burners, well characterised fuels and real composite fuels; the measurement method is described by Bryant and Bundy (2019) in NIST Technical Note 2077. Experiments are grouped into projects, among them design fires for residential and office items (51 experiments), kitchen room fires, cross-laminated timber compartments, steel-concrete composite floors under fire, vertical flame spread on parallel panels (70), thermal runaway of lithium-polymer batteries (26), NRC electrical cabinets (68), and wildland-urban interface work such as eaves and vents, structure separation shed burns, smoke characterisation, burning vehicles on pine straw and tall trees. Each experiment can be searched by title, specimen, fuel type and ignition. Coverage: laboratory experiments at NIST, with no geographic scope. Access: web pages per project and experiment with downloadable data, a user guide, and the NIST data record DOI 10.18434/mds2-2314 (version 1.0.2). Licence: NIST open data licence; free. Caveats: results reflect the specific specimens, ventilation and ignition of each test. Simulation uses are design fire inputs for fire engineering and evacuation models and fuel data for wildland-urban interface fire spread. Related records: NIST FDS and Smokeview, and NIST CONTAM.
